newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German security police hid Olympic doping.
newsitem.headline: East German security police hid Olympic doping.

text.p: Communist East Germany set up a clandestine medical facility outside the Olympic Village at the 1976 Montreal Games where athletes were given performance- enhancing steroids, German officials said on Monday.
The state authority examining documents left behind after unification by the Ministry for State Security (Stasi) said it had evidence East Germany had been particularly meticulous in Montreal.
After the games, the Stasi "dumped 10 suitcases of drugs and hypodermic syringes in the St. Laurence River", Peter Busse, director of the authority, told German radio.
Busse said the paraphernalia was partially destroyed before disposal "so that no-one would know where they came from in case they were found".
East Germany won 90 medals at the Montreal games, including 40 gold medals, second only to the Soviet Union.

The authority had years ago uncovered evidence that East German athletes had received steroids. But the new findings showed East Germany was especially well organised in its efforts to win Olympic medals.
Busse called for compensation for East German athletes who were coerced into taking steroids to improve their performance.
"There is a whole group of athletes in East Germany that without justification was thrown to the dogs," he said.
